column1: # Di Teodoro, Posti, Ogle, Fraternali & Marasco 2023, MNRAS 518, 6340 (arXiv:2207.02906), 'Dark matter halos and scaling relations of extremely massive
# spiral galaxies from extended HI rotation curves': Table 'tab:sample' (properties of the sample) joined with Table 'tab:dynquant' (derived quantities, table_dyn.tex).
# Transcribed 2026-09-28 from the arXiv LaTeX source (e-print 10509160 bytes, sha256 0fde3002bc6ca69d...; table_dyn.tex sha256 50a14956ccddb13a...), fetched with the
# owner's approval for campaign_fresh_gravity CFG40.  The rotation curves themselves are in the paper's figures only (per-galaxy atlas), not tabulated.
# Sample selection (paper Sect. 2): SDSS M_* > 1e11 Msun, ALFALFA inclination-corrected HI rotation speed > 300 km/s, inclination > 40 deg, D < 250 Mpc.
# hi_src: HI data source (new = new VLA data; WHISP; SG06 = Spekkens+2006; H13 = Hunter+2013).  D_Mpc, dD: assumed distance and error (EDD or NED).
# logMs_W1: stellar mass from WISE W1 aperture photometry (Msun; typical error 0.2 dex).  logMgas: cold gas, 1.36 M_HI (Msun; typical error 0.1 dex).
# vflat, dvflat: km/s, flat part of the HI (and where available H-alpha) rotation curve; errors include systematics on inclination, systemic velocity and centre.
# logMs_RC, dlogMs_RC: stellar mass from the rotation-curve decomposition; logMh, dlogMh: NFW halo mass (log10 Msun); logc: log10 concentration.
# flag_uncertain = 1 for NGC5635 and UGC12591: the paper states their kinematic/mass decompositions are 'extremely uncertain' and omits them from its SHMR and f_j relations;
# UGC12591 is 'an extremely massive, lenticular galaxy with relatively little gas ... barely detected in our new VLA HI data (SNR<~3 in most channels)'.
